entries.narrative:
HIS-8 (issue #224) is a DOCUMENTATION ticket with a zero-delta model, so the machine-checked core above is uninformative by construction. What it cannot express is the whole of what this ticket did, so it is recorded here.
WHAT WAS BUILT. The derived-artifact contract -- what an artifact is, what a clone inherits versus declares, when to rebuild, and the exact command -- is now stated ONCE, in skt, at skills/skt/references/derived-artifacts.md. The three other units that instruct agents about homes link to it and deliberately do not restate it.
THE MEASURED ALTERNATIVE THAT WAS REJECTED. Restating the contract in each of the four units would have made every one of them self-sufficient. It was rejected because this epic has already measured what a second copy does: DEF-021 found eight javadocs describing code that had moved, and this ticket's own BEFORE judged read found git-issue-workflow/references/skill-homes.md asserting -- in the present tense, with a measurement -- that `home verify` REFUSES a lazy clone and that the gap is unfixable. Re-measured 2026-08-23: cold shim, exit 86, `home verify` exit 0. That page was corrected, and then a second read found a TWIN passage 100 lines below it that had been left stale. Two copies of one claim, one corrected, one not, inside the fix for exactly that failure mode. That is the argument for single-sourcing, made by the ticket's own material rather than asserted.
HOW CORRECTNESS WAS DECIDED. The goal's clause 2 is a judged read, and it was run three times against three fresh agents with NO source access, each given only the four units' markdown and required to cite a file and a quoted sentence per answer. BEFORE: 0 of 3. AFTER: 3 of 3, twice, by different agents. Transcripts and scoring: results/epic-home-integrity-sync/tickets/HIS-8/judged-read/.
Clause 1's instrument moved 0 of 4 -> 4 of 4 instructing units. Both halves, and the honest limits of each, are in the goal contribution.
WHAT THIS TICKET FOUND BY MEASURING RATHER THAN READING. Two facts the source alone would have got wrong, both now on the page: building a `cli-shim` also provisions the tree behind it (stale 13 -> 11 on one build, exit 0), and a `pip:` dependency already satisfied on the ambient PATH DEFEATS its own producer -- `build` exits 1 with "the producer ran and this home still does not hold the artifact". The second is a real limit of the remedy this page recommends, filed as a deferred finding rather than papered over.
CLOSE TAKEN UNDER --allow-open, AND WHY. `close ticket` requires ticket_plan.yaml status in {accepted, closed, complete, completed, done}. This epic marks a landed ticket `delivered`, which is not in that set, and the ticket agent stops at PR OPEN by rule 7 -- so no honest status available to me satisfies the gate. `--allow-open` is the flag whose stated purpose is exactly this case, it is RECORDED and never refused, and the close is therefore the modeled state CloseTicketWeakened rather than CloseTicket. Recorded here so the terminal evaluation reads the weaker claim, not the stronger one. Filed as a deferred finding against the vocabulary mismatch itself.
NOT DONE. Ticket current == desired (verified by diff, byte-identical), so promotion carries nothing. `refinement.measured` is false because no TLC run was made: the model is byte-identical before and after, and running TLC to reproduce a number that cannot have changed would be evidence theatre.

entries.justification:
COMPLEXITY INCREASED IN THE MODULE THIS TICKET TOUCHED, and the ledger's own delta says zero because its declared model is SkillManager.tla, which is untouched. Stating the real number rather than accepting the convenient one: HomeIntegrityInternal went from 10 variables / 8 actions / 6 configurations to 28 variables / 23 actions / 18 configurations, and the healthy run from 10 distinct states to 24,000.
THE ESSENTIAL BEHAVIOUR THE ADDED REPRESENTATION CARRIES. Nine properties this epic FIXED in production and that nothing anywhere asserted: a tree identical to the live source is disposable whatever its record names (HIS-1), a divergent one is not (HIS-1), one gate is surfaced in full at most once (HIS-3), an unacknowledged gate still refuses a launch (HIS-3), a reported error is a function of the live tree (HIS-4), a clone's sanction is re-derived from the parent's own store rather than granted by its record (HIS-10), a home's two axes name one home (HIS-14), an observation never repairs what it observed (HIS-13 / DEF-067), and a damaged home is never reported clean (HIS-13). Each is carried by its own disjoint variable group, each has an expected-violation configuration that fails on IT and on nothing else, and that isolation is measured rather than asserted -- see tlc/CROSSCHECK-target-removed.txt.
WHAT THE INCREASE COSTS, stated because it is the part a later reader needs: the six groups are DISJOINT, so the healthy state count is a PRODUCT. A seventh group multiplies rather than adds, and 24,000 of budgets.max_distinct_states = 50,000 is already half the ceiling. Filed as DEF-087 together with the observation that nothing runs these configurations automatically at all.

refinement.detail:
FOUR smaller representations were considered. Three were taken and one is recommended and NOT applied.
TAKEN (1): three of the five extra candidate properties were argued and DROPPED rather than modelled. HIS-9's write confinement is already External.WritesThroughOneHomeReachNoOtherHome and External.NoOwnedSurfaceNamesAnotherHome (dual_representation_rule); HIS-11's compensation is already Internal.InFlightMaterializationLeavesTheChildUnitIntact; and DEF-036 / DEF-040, both routed to this ticket as "state it as an invariant", were REFUSED because a bounded model in which the author writes both derivations cannot catch two Java methods drifting apart -- an assertion that would pass forever regardless of the code, which is the defect #217 exists to prevent. Recorded as DEF-088. That is five properties' worth of variables not added.
TAKEN (2): HIS-1's two clauses were NOT collapsed into the single equality `hi_held_back <=> (hi_unit_content # hi_live_source)`, which would have been one invariant instead of two over the same variables. Rejected because each clause has an INDEPENDENT counterexample -- the record-consulting rule and the dispose-everything rule -- and the collapsed form gives them one configuration and one report line, which is exactly the shape that lets a fix that went too far read as a fix that worked.
TAKEN (3): the HIS-1 pass is ONE action rather than a present-then-decide pair, which removes an intermediate state in which a divergent tree is not yet held back and would have forced clause 2 to be weakened to "...once the pass is done" -- a guard a broken model satisfies by never finishing a pass.
RECOMMENDED, NOT APPLIED: give each of the six property groups its OWN specification over its own variable set, following this repository's existing `two_specs_per_module` precedent, instead of one HomeIntegritySpec over all 28 variables. That turns the healthy state count from a PRODUCT of the groups into a SUM. It was not applied because the single healthy specification is what lets HomeIntegrityInternal.cfg check all thirteen invariants in one run against a home that reaches all of their antecedents, which the two reachability probes then demonstrate; splitting it needs six healthy configurations and a decision about where the cross-group reachability probe lives. Advisory, unapproved, and named as the decision most likely to look wrong at the next extension.

entries.narrative:
results/epic-home-integrity-sync/tickets/HIS-5/goal-contribution.md is the narrative ledger. Read section 3 first -- it is the part the machine-checked core above cannot express.
THE FINDING THIS TICKET IS ACTUALLY ABOUT. TLC reports the FIRST invariant it finds violated, in an order the author does not control, so a configuration written to refute invariant X can be refuting invariant Y for years and read identically in every transcript. "The regression cfg fails" is therefore a claim about iteration order, not about the invariant. Every one of the fourteen expected-violation configurations here was consequently re-run with its TARGET REMOVED and the other thirteen invariants kept, and had to come back green. Fourteen greens. That is vacuity-ledger mechanism A answered by measurement rather than by reading a trace, and it is the check a reviewer should attack first -- transcript at tlc/CROSSCHECK-target-removed.txt.
THE SAME QUESTION FACING THE OTHER WAY. Nine invariants that HOLD is not the claim that nine were EVALUATED: every one is an implication or an equality, and an implication whose antecedent is unreachable is TRUE and worthless. This view has already nearly shipped that exact defect once -- ARTI-22's ProjectionSourceIsDecidable had "foreign" unassigned and TLC could not distinguish it from TRUE. Two reachability probes were added, following External.NoWorktreeEditEverReachesTheRootHome, and BOTH MUST FAIL; the second one's counterexample is a nine-state trace in which the antecedent of every remaining new invariant is live at once.
THREE THINGS I AM NOT CONFIDENT ABOUT, in the order a reviewer should test them. (1) NOTHING RUNS THESE CONFIGURATIONS -- run_tlc.sh has no caller in test_graph, in pytest or in CI, and the graphs are suspended on push and PR, so the manifest's expected_violations map is a table only a human re-running eighteen commands can falsify. An assertion nobody runs is the same defect as an assertion that cannot fail, one level up. DEF-087. (2) The HIS-11 omission is the weakest of the two: a write witness would make it statable, the way External.sync_history was added for exactly this reason, and I did not add one. (3) AnObservationNeverRepairsWhatItObserved is TRUE of the desired instrument and FALSE of the shipped one, because DEF-067 is open -- so specs/current now asserts something the product does not do, and specs/current and specs/desired_program_model are byte-identical for this module, which leaves the distinction nowhere to live.

refinement.detail:
Searched twice, and the second search found something the first did not.
FIRST PASS (structural, and it still holds for the model): HIS-19 changes no TLA+ module, no .cfg, no adapter and no spec double. Its conflict keys declare `tla: []` and `adapters: []`, and the assignment records `tlc: "N/A: HIS-5 carries the model work for this epic"`. `uv run pytest specs/` is green at 88 passed after the rebase onto HIS-5. The change is below the modelled surface: which absolute path string is written into a generated bash file. Adding a state variable for "the spelling of a pin" to justify a refinement record would be inventing model surface to fill a field.
SECOND PASS, IN THE PROGRAM, AND IT REMOVED REPRESENTATION. The review of #250 (MAJOR 2) asked whether the `PATH_ALIAS` arm earned its safety claim. Measured, it did not -- and neither did the claim. Removed: one `Source` enum value, one candidate-generation loop, the `Function<String,String> env` parameter threaded through `forPin`/`choose`/`candidates`, and the test helper that fed it. Removed separately (m4): the identity gate in `rejection`, which every candidate now makes unreachable.
The class is smaller and STRICTLY MORE CONSTRAINED afterwards: it reads no environment at all, so `choose` is a function of the located path and the filesystem, and the same command writes the same pin from cron and from a login shell. That is a refinement in the sense that matters here -- fewer reachable states, one fewer input -- and it was found by a reviewer asking whether a documented property was true rather than by a complexity metric, which could not see it.
KEPT DELIBERATELY: the `DurableCliPin.Source` enum, now four values. It exists so a probe can name the branch it exercises (vacuity mechanism D). Collapsing it to a boolean was reconsidered at this review and rejected again: V2/V3/V7/V14 are only distinguishable because the branches are named apart, and row 18 of the vacuity ledger is what happens when a branch has no name of its own.

entries.narrative:
HIS-19 (issue #246) / DEF-027 fixes the CAUSE under DEF-012. The machine-checked core above is uninformative by construction -- the model delta is zero because no model was touched. The full record is results/epic-home-integrity-sync/tickets/HIS-19/goal-contribution.md; this is the part the delta cannot express, written AFTER the review of PR #250 so it states the corrected position rather than the one I opened with.
WHAT WAS BROKEN. `home shims` recorded the located build's absolute path, and on a Homebrew install that path is inside the keg. The 0.24.0 upgrade deleted that directory on the operator's own machine. The generated entrypoint stayed present and executable -- so every `-x` test, including HomeDescriptor.locateCli's, called the home healthy -- while running it could only produce exit 127, and `home verify` returned EXIT 0. HIS-12 stopped remedies naming a dead pin; HIS-13 detects and repairs one. Neither stopped this class writing the same pin again, so the repair ran on a treadmill.
WHAT WAS BUILT. DurableCliPin: given the located build, find another SPELLING of the same file that carries no version segment, and pin that. `home verify` gained the one question its walk structurally could not ask -- a dead pin names a path OUTSIDE the home, and missingReferencesIn only considers paths inside it -- and now exits 1 on it, through HIS-13's reader. Existing homes migrate through HIS-13's repairer, which already re-pins by calling LauncherShims.write.
WHAT THE REVIEW CHANGED, AND IT IS THE MOST USEFUL THING IN THIS ENTRY. The class shipped with a third arm that searched PATH for a versionless entry, and a javadoc sentence claiming a substitution "cannot produce" an older build answering. The review challenged the sentence for that arm. Reproducing it confirmed the arm was unsafe -- and asking the same question of the DERIVABLE Homebrew arm showed the sentence false there too, which is more than the review claimed and is my own claim falsified by my own measurement (probes/his-19/downgrade.out, case B: `brew link` an older keg and the pin runs BUILD 0.19.2).
So the sentence was rewritten rather than narrowed, and the PATH arm was dropped on four counts: the set of things that can move a DERIVED alias is bounded and is about this product, while an arbitrary PATH directory can be moved by anything and nix generations roll backwards by design; a PATH arm makes the written pin depend on ambient state, which is a second answer to "which build does this home run" produced by the mechanism added to remove one; the fallback when nothing is substituted is a LOUD 127 that this epic already detects (`home verify` exit 1) and repairs (`home repair --fix`), whereas a silent downgrade has none of that; and the arm had no measured user -- the only layouts ever seen are Homebrew's and a fixture written for the arm itself. The governing rule, and it is this epic's own doctrine: PREFER NO SUBSTITUTION OVER AN UNSAFE ONE.
What the design now guarantees, stated so a reader cannot take more from it than was measured: issue #61's failure -- an unrelated build the operator never chose, selected by PATH ordering at launch -- cannot occur, because nothing is resolved at launch and every recorded path is the package manager's own alias for this formula. It does NOT guarantee the build never moves backwards. A deliberate downgrade is followed, and there is now a test asserting that limit rather than prose denying it.
THE OTHER REVIEW FINDING WORTH RECORDING. The reader-disagreement I had caught by hand -- `home shims` printing the located pin while writing the durable one -- was still caught only by hand. Reverting the fix reddened NOTHING in 1402 cases. The 0.24.0 upgrade deleted that directory on the operator's own machine. HIS-12 stopped remedies naming a dead pin; HIS-13 detects and repairs one. Neither stopped this class writing the same pin again, so the repair ran on a treadmill.

DurableCliPin: given the located build, find another SPELLING of the same file that carries no version segment, and pin that. `home verify` gained the one question its walk structurally could not ask -- a dead pin names a path OUTSIDE the home, and missingReferencesIn only considers paths inside it -- and now exits 1 on it, through HIS-13's reader. Existing homes migrate through HIS-13's repairer, which already re-pins by calling LauncherShims.write.
WHAT THE REVIEW CHANGED, AND IT IS THE MOST USEFUL THING IN THIS ENTRY. The class shipped with a third arm that searched PATH for a versionless entry, and a javadoc sentence claiming a substitution "cannot produce" an older build answering. The review challenged the sentence for that arm. Reproducing it confirmed the arm was unsafe -- and asking the same question of the DERIVABLE Homebrew arm showed the sentence false there too, which is more than the review claimed and is my own claim falsified by my own measurement (probes/his-19/downgrade.out, case B: `brew link` an older keg and the pin runs BUILD 0.19.2).
So the sentence was rewritten rather than narrowed, and the PATH arm was dropped on four counts: the set of things that can move a DERIVED alias is bounded and is about this product, while an arbitrary PATH directory can be moved by anything and nix generations roll backwards by design; a PATH arm makes the written pin depend on ambient state, which is a second answer to "which build does this home run" produced by the mechanism added to remove one; the fallback when nothing is substituted is a LOUD 127 that this epic already detects (`home verify` exit 1) and repairs (`home repair --fix`), whereas a silent downgrade has none of that; and the arm had no measured user -- the only layouts ever seen are Homebrew's and a fixture written for the arm itself. The governing rule, and it is this epic's own doctrine: PREFER NO SUBSTITUTION OVER AN UNSAFE ONE.
What the design now guarantees, stated so a reader cannot take more from it than was measured: issue #61's failure -- an unrelated build the operator never chose, selected by PATH ordering at launch -- cannot occur, because nothing is resolved at launch and every recorded path is the package manager's own alias for this formula. entries.narrative: HIS-20 (issue #247) is a MEASUREMENT-AND-DOCUMENTATION ticket with a zero-delta model, so the machine-checked core above is uninformative by construction. WHAT WAS MEASURED. Six judged reads before any documentation change and six after, twelve different agents, one per (tier, direction, phase). Each was sandboxed to a read-only copy of ONE home tier's unit markdown, forbidden to read source or run any skill-manager/skt command, and required to cite a file and a quoted sentence per answer or say NOT ANSWERABLE FROM THE CORPUS. Transcripts, per-question scoring and the change-management table: results/epic-home-integrity-sync/tickets/HIS-20/judged-read/. THE FINDING UNDERNEATH EVERY SCORE, and it is not a documentation finding. Two of the three home tiers put ZERO units in front of an agent that document the tier model. The project home and every worktree cloned from it held deploy-helm, spec-double-compiler, test-graph and tracing-observability, and no plugins -- not skt, not skill-manager, not git-issue-workflow. Every correct answer both lower-tier BEFORE readers gave about tiers traces to ~18 lines of spec-double-compiler/references/runtime_requirements.md, a consumer skill documenting the home system incidentally to explain where tlc2 comes from. And this repository's own skill-project.toml ALREADY DECLARED skt and skill-manager; the home had simply never been resolved against it, projects/ empty in both. One `project resolve` closed it and turned eleven PARTIAL/FAIL cells into PASS. So the lower-tier gap is PROVISIONING, not prose, and no documentation change this ticket could make would have closed it: this ticket owns no unit those homes held. Escalated as DEF-096. WHAT THE PROSE ACTUALLY CLOSED, separately from that. Exit 79 ("refusing to run against a home you did not name", DEF-018) appeared in ZERO of the four instructing units' markdown -- measured with a validated grep, 0 files against a control term matching 19 -- and the root BEFORE read answered the question confidently with exits 5 and 6 instead. It is now stated once. DEF-077's conflict between the documented publish route and every epic brief's containment rule is stated as a SPLIT rather than a block, and the AFTER worktree read walked it exactly, including the reporting obligation. And the unit-name-to-repository mapping, which no command prints, now names where it is recorded. THE READS CHANGED THE FIX, WHICH IS THE POINT OF RUNNING THEM. Two AFTER readers were invited to say the expansion went too far and both did, naming the same passages. One found that the measurement sentence this ticket had just added was true of the home BEFORE `project resolve` and false of the home the reader was standing in -- the epic's founding defect reproduced inside the fix for it, in under a day. Another found that the false half of the skt PATH claim lived inside the snippet skt tells you to paste into every project's AGENTS.md, so the correction stayed at root while the falsehood travelled. Both fixed. A third of the recent expansion was cut on their evidence, including a section of workflows.md that re-derived projects.md sentence for sentence while itself saying "point there, do not re-derive it". A SENTENCE THIS TICKET WROTE AND THEN MEASURED WRONG. Its first draft said the repository URL "lives in units.lock.toml and in installed/<unit>.json". Root records origin for 29 of 29 lock entries; a resolved worktree home for 4 of 6, the two missing being exactly the units `project resolve` installed. Corrected to name the per-unit record; the CLI gap filed as DEF-100. HONEST LIMITS. The doc-only sandbox is not airtight: every subagent's system prompt carries a ~40-skill listing in which skt's own description states the three-tier model verbatim. All six AFTER readers were asked to itemize that contamination and did. n = 1 per condition. Two of the three AFTER corpora exist nowhere on disk -- the root overlay is a sandbox until two leaf PRs merge and sync, and the project corpus is an explicitly labelled counterfactual. Four cells stay PARTIAL or FAIL after the fix and are named as failures. NOT DONE. Ticket current == desired, so promotion carries nothing. refinement.measured is false because the model is byte-identical before and after, and running TLC to reproduce a number that cannot have changed would be evidence theatre.
